parts.why: Times are right and A/B are equal (10:00, 3:00 / 5:00, 8:00). But the key does not draw the hands: it only writes „10:00“ in small red digits in the middle of the clock face (enlarged). A key for a drawing task must show the short hour hand on 10 and the long minute hand on 12 (same for 3:00, 5:00, 8:00). Fix: draw both hands in the key.

Form B cards overlap: B1 is Montag–Dienstag–Mittwoch and B2 is Sonntag–Montag–Dienstag, so each card's answer is printed on the other card („Montag“ is the heute of B2 and the answer of B1; „Dienstag“ the reverse). The child can copy spelling and order; form A (Mittwoch–Donnerstag–Freitag / Samstag–Sonntag–Montag) has no overlap, so B is easier. Fix: B2 heute = „Samstag“ (answers Freitag | Sonntag) or any day not adjacent to B1.

Key sums are right (A 5+2+2=9, 5+1=6; B 5+2+1=8, 5+2=7). Three defects: (1) „Zähle die Münzen“ literally asks for the number of coins, so a child can defend 3 and 2 instead of 9 and 6; (2) the direction names a „Geldbeutel“ that is not drawn; (3) the coins are pink discs with a bare digit, no „ct“, no copper colour, not recognisable as Euro coins, so the part is plain addition, not money. Fix: draw 1-, 2-, 5-Cent coins (copper, with „Cent“) and use the direction in the instruction block. „Betrag“ is also a hard word for Klasse 1 read-aloud.
43+28=71 and 47+15=62, both with Zehnerübergang, same difficulty; empty Rechenstrich on the child page. Note for the key: other jump paths (e.g. +7, +20, +1) are also right.
66−27=39 and 64−28=36, both with Zehnerübergang; equal.

The direction says „Wenn die Frage fehlt, schreibe eine passende Frage auf“, but in both forms the question is printed („Frage: Wie viele Zitronen sind jetzt in der Kiste?“). It also says „jede Sachaufgabe“ for one card. The key gives „Antwort: 71“ / „84“; in a Frage-Rechnung-Antwort lesson Klasse 2 writes an Antwortsatz. Fix: direction „Lies die Sachaufgabe. Schreibe die Rechnung und einen Antwortsatz auf.“ and key „Antwort: Jetzt sind 71 Zitronen in der Kiste.“ / „Jetzt sind 84 Orangen in der Kiste.“ (Or really leave the question out in both forms if the lesson's skill is to be tested.)
A cylinder → Körper box, B parallelogram → flat box; one right answer each. Only one card per form, so „Verbinde jede Form“ should read „die Form“.
Checked every row of Tulpe, Regenschirm, Krabbe and Sonne cell by cell against the axis: all four keys are exact mirror images; 23/20 vs 22/25 cells, equal effort.

Form B uses the same silhouette (the down arrow) and the same three options as A, only shuffled (A: right, up, down; B: down, up, right): B asks exactly what A asks. And the choice needs no tangram thinking, only „which arrow points down“. Fix: a different silhouette in B, and in both forms an asymmetric figure (e.g. cat, boat) whose distractors are its mirror image and a rotation, so „gedreht oder gespiegelt“ really has to be checked.
Key fields correct (A C1, D4, E4, F5; B B1, C1, F4, C5); A and B equal. „in der Farbe seiner Gruppe“ is odd when there is one group; see instruction.

Order is right (A Delfin 1, Leopard 2, Pferd 3, Tiger 4; B Birne 1, Grapefruit 2, Mango 3, Zitrone 4). But the direction „Nur nummerieren: vier Karten von 1 bis 4.“ does not say to order by the Abc; read aloud to Klasse 1 it is not a task. Fix the direction (see instruction). Minor: the tiger and leopard pictures look almost alike; harmless because the words are printed.

Each form has one word and both are nouns (ELCH, KIWI); the Verben box is never the answer, so a child who puts everything under Nomen scores full marks, and the lesson is „Nomen und Verben“. Fix: two words per form, one noun and one verb, e.g. A „ELCH, SCHWIMMEN“, B „KIWI, LAUFEN“. Also say whether the child must write the noun with a capital (key shows „Elch“).

Keys are right (langweilig, müde, sicher, eckig) and each has one opposite. Grade fit: „riskant“ (B1 distractor) and „munter“ are not Klasse-1 vocabulary; a child who cannot read „riskant“ cannot rule it out. B also has the answer in first position on both cards. Fix: replace B1 with a Klasse-1 triple, e.g. „nass → feucht / trocken / warm“ (answer trocken, in position 2 or 3).

Keys are right. The hint chips say „Satzanfang · Namen · Satzzeichen“, but the words to capitalise are Nomen (Delfine, Suchbild, Papayas, Geschichte), and form B has no name at all; the lesson is „Satzanfang, Nomen und Satzzeichen“. Chip must read „Nomen“. B's sentence „Oma mag die Papayas in der Geschichte“ is unnatural; use e.g. „oma kauft im laden zwei papayas“ → „Oma kauft im Laden zwei Papayas.“ „In jedem Satz“ for one sentence → „In diesem Satz“.

One word per form, both nouns (Schildkröte, Granatapfel), printed with a capital letter and a picture beside them: the capital alone gives „Nomen“, and Verben/Adjektive are never tested. Fix: three words per form, one of each kind, printed all lower-case or all caps, e.g. A „schildkröte, kriechen, langsam“, B „granatapfel, essen, süß“.

A1 shows two white chickens; a German child says „Hühner“, and „Die Hühner picken Körner im Hof.“ is the most natural sentence, so the key „Hennen“ is not the only right answer (the label „Henne“ is printed but the direction asks only for „das Wort für mehrere“). Labels are on A1 only, not on A2/B1/B2. Fix: print the singular under every picture and say „Schreibe das Wort unter dem Bild in der Mehrzahl“; or replace the hen by an animal with one name. B2 horses look like foals; accept „Ponys/Fohlen“ or use a clearer picture.
singst, wandert, springt, lachst are right; equal level (du + 3rd person). „Jeden Sonntag wandert Emma im Park“ is a bit odd (one wanders in the Wald or Berge); „im Wald“ would read more naturally.

Keys are right, but (1) the pictures contradict the sentences: a waitress for „Lina sieht die Fähre“, a janitor with a broom for „Leon schläft um sieben Uhr“, a coach, a teacher for „Anna spielt in der Garage“; remove them or use matching ones. (2) B1 „Max schläft um acht Uhr“ is A2 „Leon schläft um sieben Uhr“ with a new name and number; give B1 a different Wann-sentence, e.g. „Max kommt am Montag.“ → „Wann kommt Max?“ (3) Key should accept „Um wie viel Uhr schläft Leon?“ as well.

Answer tell: the dashed box is one letter wide in A (Man_el → t) and two letters wide in B (Bu__er → tt), so the box size gives the answer (enlarged both). Each form has one item and they test opposite cases. B's butter is drawn as a yellow block with holes; children say „Käse“ or „Schwamm“. The „Regel im Kasten“ is not written, the box only shows „tt · Bett · Blatt“. Fix: equal-width boxes; two items per form (one t, one tt); a recognisable butter picture or another tt word (Mutter, Kette, Ratte); write the rule in one short line.
Fisch → fischen (Fibel, Fieber only share letters), Zelt → zelten (Zebra, Zettel); one answer each, pictures clear.

Keys right (Bild, Zahl). Grade fit: „Bildhauer, abbilden, bildlich“ and „zahlreich, Bezahlung“ are Klasse 3-4 words; Klasse 2 can only find the common letters without knowing the family. The direction names a „Stein“ that is drawn as a plain dashed box. Fix: Klasse-2 family words, e.g. A „Bilderbuch, Wandbild, bildlich“ → keep max. one hard word; B „Zahlenreihe, zählen, Lieblingszahl“, and say „in das leere Kästchen“.

Keys right (unehrlich, unecht, unreif, ungerecht). The direction says „Setze die Vorsilbe vor jedes Wort“ but „un-“ appears nowhere on the card (checked the child page); the lesson covers un-, ein-, aus-, um-. Fix: name it in the direction („Setze die Vorsilbe un- …“) or print „un-“ on the card.
verblüfft/erstaunt, müde/schläfrig, winzig/klein, köstlich/lecker; one pair each, pictures clear (surprised face, tired face, ant, cake).

Keys right. Tell: A2 „erstaunt → verblüfft“ is the exact pair the child just circled in part 1 A1 (verblüfft + erstaunt), so it can be copied. Fix: another A2 pair, e.g. „leise → still“ with distractors „groß, witzig, köstlich“.

A „flott – schnell – blitzschnell“: Duden gives „flott“ = „schnell, zügig“, so flott 1 / schnell 2 can be argued either way; two orders are defensible. B „knabbern 1, essen 2, verschlingen 3“ is fine. Fix A with a clear scale, e.g. „kühl – kalt – eiskalt“.
stottert (Ist … ist …), flüstert (ins Ohr), schluchzt (Tränen), jammert (complaint); each is the best fit. Direction wording can be smoother, see instruction.

Both forms use the same story „Ben backt Brötchen“ with one question each (A Wer → Papa, B Warum → „Oma mag Brötchen sehr gern“). If A is used before and B after the unit, B is a reread; and one literal question is thin for „Eine Geschichte lesen und Fragen beantworten“. Fix: a second story of the same length for B, two or three questions per form; „bei jeder Frage“ then fits.
Elefant / Giraffe / Affe and Eule / Fuchs / Kaninchen are the only fits by article and meaning; picture order differs from gap order, distractors (Traktor, Taxi, Bus, Flugzeug) clear.

Key right (Pinguin 2, Eidechse 4 Beine), but the only task is counting legs; there is no Steckbrief to read, which is trivially below Klasse 2 and does not test the lesson „Ein Tier-Steckbrief“. Fix: two or three rows per animal, e.g. „Lebensraum: Wald / Meer und Eis / Wüste“, „Nahrung: Fisch / Gras / Nüsse“.

A practises t and u, B f and i: the f (loop above and below the line) is the hardest letter of the Ausgangsschrift, so B is harder. The direction „schreibe dann jeden Buchstaben verbunden allein bis zum Ende der Zeile und in den leeren Zeilen darunter“ is contradictory („verbunden“ vs „allein“) and there is one empty line, not several. Fix: letters of equal difficulty in both forms (e.g. B „i“ and „n“, or A also gets an f/h), new direction, and name the script on the teacher page (VA or LA), since schools using SAS or Grundschrift write these letters differently.

The item and its box show the identical picture (pig → pig box, cat → cat box, orange → orange box, pomegranate → pomegranate box), so this is picture matching, not sorting („Was gehört zusammen?“). The lookalike boxes make it a trick instead: the leopard cub icon looks like the orange cat, the red apple like the pomegranate (enlarged). Fix: category boxes (e.g. Bauernhof / Zoo, or Obst / Gemüse, or by colour) and an item that is a different member of one category.
8, 5 / 9, 4 in the Zehnerfeld, counted; equal.
1 < 6 and 8 > 4 are right. Thin: one card per form and „=“ (gleich viele, in the lesson title) is never the answer; consider a second card with equal groups.
Missing 2., 3., 4., 7. / 2., 3., 4., 6.; right and equal.
8 = 7 + 1 and 9 = 1 + 8 are right; both are ±1 decompositions, equal.
All four Aufgabenfamilien correct (9/2/7, 7/4/3, 10/6/4, 7/2/5).
3, 6 / 7, 5; one plus and one minus Platzhalter per form.
8−3=5 and 9−3=6, parallel stories. „Lies jede Rechengeschichte“ should be „die Rechengeschichte“; the dotted line left of the answer box is not mentioned in the direction.

Lesson is „Plus oder Minus?“, but both forms are minus pictures with the same shape of answer (A 8 − 7 = 1, B 6 − 5 = 1): the child never has to decide plus vs minus and the result is 1 both times. Fix: two pictures per form, one Dazukommen (plus) and one Wegnehmen (minus), with different results.
16 = 10 + 6 and 17 = 10 + 7, counted in the double Zehnerfeld; right.

The direction „Zeige eine Zahl von 11 bis 19 als Zehnerfeld und Strichliste.“ does not fit the card at all: the card asks for Vorgänger/Nachfolger, Zehner/Einer and „10 mehr, 10 weniger“, and has no Zehnerfeld or Strichliste. And „16 + 10 = 26“, „19 + 10 = 29“ leave the Klasse-1 Zahlenraum bis 20 that the unit title names. Fix: new direction (see instruction) and replace „10 mehr“ with something inside 20 (e.g. „Verdopple die Einer“ or only „10 weniger“).
sechzehn, zehn / siebzehn, neun with good distractors (sechs, siebzehn, fünfzehn, neunzehn).

Arrow positions measured: A 6, 13, 16 and B 7, 14, 17 are exactly where the arrows point. Two defects: the key numerals are printed twice on top of each other (19.5 pt and 16.5 pt in two colours, found in the PDF text layer) and look smeared; and the number of the day (16 in A, 17 in B) recurs as an answer in parts 1, 3 and 4 of the same form. Fix: print each key number once; choose arrow values that are not the Zahl des Tages.
6+7 = 6+4+3 = 13 and 8+4 = 8+2+2 = 12; start dot only on the child page.
7+7+1=15, 4+4+1=9 / 8+8+1=17, 3+3+1=7; the „+1“ box fixes the smaller double, so one answer each.
17−7−1=9 and 16−6−2=8; right and equal.

A „Lina hat 9 Bananen. Lina gibt 4 Bananen ab.“ = 5 stays below 10, no Zehnerübergang, while B „Mia hat 11 Äpfel … gibt 5 ab“ = 6 crosses the ten. A is easier and not „Rechengeschichten bis 20“. Fix A: e.g. „Lina hat 13 Bananen. Sie gibt 5 Bananen ab.“ → 8. Use „Sie“ for the second sentence in both forms.
17, 10 / 18, 10 are right (analogy tasks without crossing, fine for „Rechnen bis 20“). The box holds the result, so the direction should say „das Ergebnis“, not „die fehlende Zahl“.
4 Zehnerstangen + 7 Einer = 47, 5 + 3 = 53 (counted the cubes enlarged). The old „■·10 +“ notation is gone.
73|75, 40|42 / 68|70, 37|39; each form crosses a ten once.

Keys right. B1 „85 < 88“ has the same tens (the real place-value test); form A has none (82 > 75, 26 < 69 are decided by the tens). Fix A2: a same-tens or swapped-digit pair, e.g. „62 □ 26“ or „64 □ 67“.

Arrow positions measured: 47, 59 / 41, 49 are right. But every key numeral is printed twice on top of itself (19.5 pt and 16.5 pt, two colours), so it looks smeared/ghosted (enlarged 8×). Fix: one key mark.

Keys right, but A1 (79: ↓ ← ↑), A2 (52: ↓ ← ↑) and B2 (54: ↓ ← ↑) all cancel down and up, so the answer is always start − 1; a child who ignores the vertical arrows scores. B1 (68: ← ← ↓ = 76) is a real task, so B is harder than A. Fix: sequences without cancelling moves and with similar net effects in both forms, e.g. A „34: ↓ ↓ →“ = 55, B „47: ↓ ↓ ←“ = 66.
Turtle 0–5 and watermelon slice 0–7 measured against the ruler marks; right.
Airplane 4 vs skateboard 7 → 3; book 3 vs stapler 4 → 1; the boxes are pre-shaded on the child page.

Hands checked: 8:40, 6:05 / 10:05, 5:05 are right. But both B clocks have the minute hand on the 1 (two times „:05“), while A has 8:40, where the hour hand is almost at 9 (the real difficulty, with distractor 9:40). B is easier and repeats itself. Fix B2: e.g. 3:50 with distractors 4:50 and 10:15.

Tallies 4 and 7 / 3 and 4 are right, but the key draws no bars: it prints tiny red digits („4“, „7“) floating below the matching grid line (enlarged). Fix: shade the correct bars in the key. (The persimmon in B looks like a tomato; harmless, it is a label only.)

Counts right (A 4, 1, 5; B 3, 5, 1). Tell: in A the column above 5 has 5 X, so „5 → 5“ is right by copying the label. Fix: give that column 3 or 6 X. The plot also has no question or title saying what was counted.
4 horses → 8, 6 reindeer → 12; 7 watermelons → 14, 1 avocado → 2. „echte Anzahl“ reads oddly; see instruction.

Keys right (A all circles: star unmöglich, circle sicher, square unmöglich; B triangles + one star: triangle möglich, star möglich, square unmöglich). But A never asks „möglich“ and B never asks „sicher“: the forms test different words, and with one bag per form both cannot occur. Fix: two bags per form (one with one kind only, one mixed) so each form has sicher, möglich and unmöglich. The container is drawn like a jar with a lid; draw a bag or say „Glas“.
5 rows of 4 → 5 · 4 = 20; 3 rows of 6 → 3 · 6 = 18. Right.
22 : 3 = 7 R 1 and 22 : 5 = 4 R 2; right, Klasse 3 notation.
4 + 14 = 9 + 9 and 4 + 12 = 15 + 1; one answer each.

Keys right (699 + 518: ungerade; 683 + 229: gerade). The table lists „gerade + ungerade = ungerade“ but A asks ungerade + gerade, a row the table does not have, while the direction says „nutze die Tabelle“; B's case is in the table. Fix: add „ungerade + gerade = ungerade“ as a fourth row.

In both forms the right angle is the only one drawn as an upright „L“, and the two acute angles in A are identical. A child picks the L shape without knowing the concept. Fix: show the right angle turned (e.g. 30° or 45°) in at least one form and add an angle of about 80° or 100° as a distractor.

Both forms have one card and both answers are „kein Rechteck“ (parallelogram, trapezoid); „Rechteck“ is never right and the hint „Auch Quadrate sind Rechtecke“ is never needed. Fix: two cards per form, one square or rectangle (→ Rechteck) and one non-rectangle.

Keys right (A square 4, regular hexagon 6, rectangle 2; B regular pentagon 5, square 4, equilateral triangle 3; measured the shapes). In B every answer equals the number of corners, so counting corners scores 3/3; A has only the rectangle to catch that strategy. Fix: in both forms at least two shapes whose axes differ from their corners (rectangle 2, rhombus 2, isosceles triangle 1, kite 1).
6 pandas → 30, 2 fish → 10; 7 pineapples → 35, 3 blackberries → 15.

The lesson is „halbe Schritte am Zahlenstrahl“, but every X sits above a whole number and every question asks a whole number, so 1½, 2½, 3½ are never used. Tells: A „2 → 2“, B „1 → 1“ and „4 → 4“ (count equals the label). Fix: put X above half-step marks and ask about them; avoid counts equal to the label.
A star: 3 of 6 vs 1 of 6 → left bag; B circle: 3 of 6 vs 4 of 6 → right bag. Right (counted enlarged). The bags look like jars with lids.
Schild-krö-te 3, Ze-bra 2 / Ap-fel 2, Zi-tro-ne 3; pictures are named that way by children; the note that the number of arcs counts is helpful.

A2 shows a red coiled snake; a German first grader says „Schlange“, not „Kobra“, and finds no „schla“ among „ko / ke / ku“. Fix: a picture whose everyday name starts with „Ko“, e.g. Koala („Ko-a-la“) or Kokosnuss. Robot („Ro-bo-ter“), Raupe („rau“) and Gitarre („gi“) are fine.

A1 „Tiger“: the key fills five boxes T-i-g-e-r, but the final „er“ is one sound; a child who writes four sounds (T-i-g-er or „Tiga“, the very spelling part 4 accepts) is right too. And B is easier: „Wal“ has 3 sounds, no cluster, against A's „Wolf“ (4, with lf). The wolf can also be read as „Hund“. Fix: A1 a word without -er (e.g. „Nase“, „Sofa“), B2 a four-sound word with a cluster (e.g. „Hund“ only if the picture is a dog, or „Wurm“).
Kamel, Panda / Tiger, Delfin; lautgetreu scoring note is right for Klasse 1.

Kuh, Hund / Hahn, Wal; the article and the meaning leave one word each. Note: the picture beside the sentence already shows the answer, so the sentence need not be read; B2 „bläst eine Wasserfontäne“ is harder to decode than A's sentences.

Only one order each („Die Giraffen sind bunt.“, „Emma sieht zwei Feigen.“), but giraffes are not „bunt“: the model sentence states something false next to a giraffe picture. Fix A: „Die Giraffen sind groß.“ (words „Giraffen / sind / Die / groß.“).

Keys right (Wo, Was / Was, Wo), but (1) „Wer“ is never the answer in either form although the lesson is „wer, was, wo“; (2) the pictures still contradict the sentences (a chef in a kitchen for „Finn ist am Fluss“, a carpenter for „Finn malt den Krankenwagen“, a runner for „Lea liest im Wald“), as the first review reported. Fix: three cards per form (Wer, Was, Wo), e.g. „Mia malt ein Bild.“ with „Mia“ marked; remove the pictures or use matching ones.
Apple eaten to the core; paper strips → paper chain. One fitting frame each, distractors clear.

One word per form and each form tests one field (A hüpfen → gehen, B gaffen → sehen), so a guess has 50%. „gaffen“ is pejorative (rubbernecking) and a poor model word for Klasse 3. Fix: two words per form, one for each field, e.g. A „schleichen, beobachten“, B „stolpern, starren“; replace „gaffen“.
Lehrerin + Bäcker / Näherin + Sänger: now each form has one -erin and one -er with a vowel change; pictures match the gender.

Keys right (herzen, witzig: only the verb / adjective fits). The direction „Schreibe jedes Wort von den vier Karten in den Satz, in den es passt“ implies four sentences; there is one sentence and only one card goes in. Also „herzen“ is old-fashioned; most children say „knuddeln“, so A is harder than B. Fix: direction „Welches Wort von den vier Karten passt in den Satz? Schreibe es in die Lücke.“; for A a family whose verb children use, e.g. „Spiel: spielen, Spieler, verspielt, Spielplatz“ → „Die Kinder ___ im Hof.“ (spielen).

Ball → er, Emma → sie / Banane → sie, Paul → er are right, but „es“ is never the answer in either form, so a child who never circles „es“ scores. Fix: a third card per form with a neuter noun, e.g. A „Buch → es“, B „Fahrrad → es“ (or „Mädchen → es“ as the harder item in both).

Keys right, but A crosses the order (Lisa first, „Er“ → Till second) while B keeps it (Henri first, „Er“ → Henri): a child who links first to first gets B right and A wrong. Fix: same pattern in both forms (crossed). Minor: B shows a male doctor and a female nurse; swapping them avoids the stereotype.
Dreieck: only the right triangle (the two curved shapes and the quadrilateral are not); Quadrat: only the square (parallelogram, rectangle, open square are not).

Same problem as the ruling: the silhouette is printed solid dark (child page checked) and the child lays real tangram pieces on or beside it, so nothing is left on the paper to mark, and the check needs a full class set of tangrams. If wanted, a fixable paper version: print the silhouette as a light outline at the size of the class tangram and ask „Zeichne die Linien zwischen den Teilen ein“; otherwise leave the part out, the check stays fair to „Formen“ through part 1.
Fish 6 and papaya 7 boxes (pre-shaded); right. „Jeder Gegenstand“ is wrong for one card and a fish; see instruction.
6 cats, 4 antelopes / 4 strawberries, 6 clementines; right.
Bars 3 and 6 / 6 and 3 read off the scale; right.

Keys right (A Specht, Elch; B Nektarine, Kiwi; patterns ABC). But „Verbinde jedes Bild mit seinem leeren Kästchen“ with four pictures and two boxes tells a Klasse-1 child to connect all four, including the two that do not belong. Fix the direction (see instruction). The key numbers the boxes 1/2 in A and 7/8 in B; harmless but inconsistent.

checks.why: All answers are right, but the clock key shows no hands, form B's weekday cards give each other's answers, and the coin part says „Zähle die Münzen“ (= 3) and shows no recognisable Euro coins.
Rechenstrich parts are good and equal; the Sachaufgabe direction mentions a missing question that is not missing and the key needs an Antwortsatz.

Symmetry and Planquadrate parts are exact; the tangram part repeats A in B and is solvable by arrow direction. Körper are covered by one card only; say on the page which four lessons are not in the check.
Abc direction does not name the task, the noun/verb part never has a verb, and „riskant“ is above Klasse 1. „Begleiter“ is in the title but has no part; the page must say so.
Four of five parts need changes: chip „Namen“ instead of „Nomen“, a word-class part with only nouns, „Hennen“ vs „Hühner“, and pictures that contradict the question sentences.
The t/tt box width gives the answer and the butter looks like cheese; the prefix un- is never named; the word-stem family words are above Klasse 2.
Good unit; one copyable pair (verblüfft/erstaunt) between parts 1 and 2 and an ambiguous strength order (flott/schnell).
A and B share one story with one question each, the Steckbrief part only counts legs, and the cursive letters are not of equal difficulty.
Number parts are right and equal; the sorting part matches identical pictures instead of sorting.
Everything is right; only the plus-or-minus part never asks for plus and gives 1 in both forms.
The Zahl-des-Tages direction describes a different task and „10 mehr“ goes beyond 20; the number-line key prints each numeral twice.
Strategy parts are exact; form A's word problem stays within 10 while B's crosses the ten.

The Hundertertafel jumps cancel out in three of four cards, form A has no same-tens comparison, and the number-line key is double-printed. The page must say that Bündeln and the Hundertertafel itself are not in the check.
Form B's clocks are both :05, the bar key draws no bars, A's line plot has „5 → 5“, and each form misses one of sicher / möglich / unmöglich.
All keys are right; the parity table needs its fourth row. Still thin: one card per part and none of the three Zahlenfolgen/Sachaufgaben lessons; say so on the page.
Four of six parts can be passed by a wrong strategy (pick the upright L, always „kein Rechteck“, count the corners, copy the label) and the half steps are never used. All fixable at the source.
Big improvement on the first review; the cobra (children say „Schlange“) and the five-box „Tiger“ remain.
English words are gone; „Die Giraffen sind bunt“ is false and the W-question part still has contradicting pictures and never asks „Wer“.
The -er/-erin part is now balanced; the pronoun parts never ask „es“ and differ in difficulty, and the word-field part tests one field per form.

Ruling lifted: the picture graph and bar graph are now in, so Formen, Messen and Diagramme are all fairly checked. The tangram part still cannot be marked on paper and should be left out (or redrawn as an outline to draw in); fix the pattern direction.

instruction.G1-233: Lies die Uhrzeit. Zeichne den kurzen Stundenzeiger und den langen Minutenzeiger in die Uhr ein.
instruction.G1-228: Wie viel Geld ist es? Rechne die Münzen zusammen und schreibe den Betrag in das Kästchen.
instruction.G2-506: Lies die Sachaufgabe. Schreibe die Rechnung und einen Antwortsatz auf.
instruction.G2-244: Verbinde die Form mit der richtigen Kiste: flache Formen links, Körper rechts.
instruction.G2-279: Finde jedes Feld mit Buchstabe und Zahl, zum Beispiel B2. Male es in der Farbe an, die daneben steht.
instruction.G1-262: Ordne die vier Wörter nach dem Abc. Schreibe 1, 2, 3 und 4 in die Kreise.
instruction.G1-293: Ist das Wort ein Nomen oder ein Verb? Schreibe jedes Wort in den richtigen Kasten. Nomen schreibst du groß.
instruction.G2-274: In diesem Satz fehlen die großen Anfangsbuchstaben und das Satzzeichen. Schreibe ihn richtig auf die Linie.
instruction.G2-349: Schau dir die Bilder an. Es sind mehrere. Schreibe das Wort unter dem Bild in der Mehrzahl in das Kästchen.
instruction.G2-315: Lies die Regel im Kasten. Sprich das Bildwort deutlich und schreibe t oder tt in das Kästchen.
instruction.G1-397: Sag, was du auf dem Bild siehst. Kreise darüber das Wort ein, das zur selben Wortfamilie gehört.
instruction.G2-375: Kreise in allen drei Wörtern den gemeinsamen Teil ein. Schreibe ihn als Nomen mit großem Anfangsbuchstaben in das leere Kästchen.
instruction.G2-320: Setze die Vorsilbe un- vor jedes Wort. Schreibe das neue Wort mit der gegenteiligen Bedeutung auf die Linie.
instruction.G2-374: Lies jeden Satz. Welches Wort aus der Sprechblase passt statt „sagt“ am besten? Schreibe es in das Kästchen.
instruction.G2-254: Lies die Geschichte genau. Kreise dann die richtige Antwort ein.
instruction.G2-377: Spure die grauen Buchstaben nach. Schreibe den Buchstaben dann verbunden weiter bis zum Ende der Zeile und in die leere Zeile darunter.
instruction.G1-240: Lies die Rechengeschichte. Die Bilder helfen dir. Schreibe die Antwort in das Kästchen.
instruction.G1-213: Lies die Rechengeschichte. Die Bilder helfen dir. Schreibe die Antwort in das Kästchen.
instruction.G1-208: Rechne jede Aufgabe im Kopf. Schreibe das Ergebnis in das Kästchen.
instruction.G1-255: Das ist die Zahl des Tages. Schreibe den Vorgänger und den Nachfolger auf, die Zehner und die Einer, und rechne die Aufgaben.
instruction.G2-238: Jedes Bild steht für 2. Schreibe auf, wie viele es in jeder Reihe wirklich sind.
instruction.G3-333: Jedes Bild steht für 5. Schreibe auf, wie viele es in jeder Reihe wirklich sind.
instruction.G3-386: Rechne nicht. Schau auf die unterstrichenen Einer, nutze die Tabelle und kreuze an, ob die Summe gerade oder ungerade ist.
instruction.G3-340: Ist es ein Rechteck? Auch Quadrate sind Rechtecke. Verbinde jede Form mit dem richtigen Kasten.
instruction.G3-397: Schreibe jedes Wort in das Wortfeld, zu dem es gehört: „gehen“ oder „sehen“.
instruction.G3-399: Welches Wort von den vier Karten passt in den Satz? Schreibe es in die Lücke.
instruction.G1-139: Wie lang ist das Bild? Zähle die Kästchen darunter und schreibe die Länge auf.
instruction.G1-155: Zwei Bilder fehlen. Welche sind es? Verbinde jedes leere Kästchen mit dem passenden Bild.
instruction.G1-160: Zu welcher Kiste gehört das Bild? Verbinde es mit der richtigen Kiste.

notes: Read all 20 dump.json files and opened all 20 contact sheets; rendered child and key pages larger for: clock key (no hands) and coin discs; plus-minus child page (question printed, empty Rechenstrich); Größen ruler, bars key, clocks, line plots, picture graph, both bags; Malnehmen parity child page; g1 shapes child page (solid tangram silhouette, shaded length boxes) and pattern key; g2 symmetry (every row of all four pictures checked against the axis) and both tangram choices; g3 angles, axes shapes, line plot, bags; sounds child page, robot/cobra, tiger/wolf; reading story B; plural pictures; t/tt boxes and butter; prefix card; cursive f/i; pronoun card; Zahlen bis 10 sorting cards; Zehnerübergang child page; Zahlen bis 100 cubes and number line.

Doubled key numerals were confirmed in the PDF text layer (same number at 19.5 pt and 16.5 pt, two colours, overlapping) in de1-zahlen-bis-20 part 4 and de2-zahlen-bis-100 part 4 (keys A and B); no other key in these 20 units has it.

Measured: number-line arrows (de1-zahlen-bis-20, de2-zahlen-bis-100) all sit exactly on the keyed numbers; the g3 'diamond' is a square turned 45° (equal diagonals), so 4 axes is right; the hexagon is regular (height 0.866 × width).

Recurring pattern across units: one card per form where only one category can ever be right (Nomen only, kein Rechteck only, er/sie without es, Was/Wo without Wer, minus only). These parts do not test the decision their lesson teaches; two or three cards per form, one per category, would fix all of them.

Fixes from the first review that are now in: Cranberrys/Jeep gone, Katze/Schwan/Fledermaus/Brombeere gone, -er/-erin balanced, Auto → es replaced, Zehner/Einer notation, ±1 direction, Platzhalter and Teilen-mit-Rest directions. Still open from the first review: contradicting pictures in the W-question part.
My render files went to a private folder (scratchpad rev-de2) because the shared rev folder was being emptied by another session; deleted when done.
